events.title: Battle of the Golden Spurs
events.description: Near Courtrai in Flanders, a force of Flemish townsmen and militia defeated a French army of heavily armored knights. The victory was won largely by common foot soldiers.
events.significance: The battle showed that disciplined infantry could beat mounted knights. It also became a lasting symbol of Flemish identity, and Flanders still celebrates it as a regional holiday.

events.title: Burr mortally wounds Hamilton in a duel
events.description: Vice President Aaron Burr shot former Treasury Secretary Alexander Hamilton during a duel at Weehawken, New Jersey. Hamilton died of his wound the following day.
events.significance: The duel cost the young United States one of its founding architects and badly damaged Burr's political career. It remains one of the best-known political confrontations in American history.

events.title: To Kill a Mockingbird is published
events.description: Harper Lee's debut novel, set in Depression-era Alabama, was first published. It tells of racial injustice through the eyes of a young girl.
events.significance: The book won the Pulitzer Prize and became a classic of American literature. It is widely taught in schools and has shaped public conversation about justice and prejudice.

events.title: Skylab returns to Earth
events.description: America's first space station fell out of orbit and broke apart over the atmosphere. Debris scattered across the Indian Ocean and parts of Western Australia.
events.significance: Skylab's fall drew worldwide attention to the risks of uncontrolled re-entry. It also marked the end of an early chapter in long-duration human spaceflight.

events.title: Srebrenica massacre begins
events.description: Bosnian Serb forces under Ratko Mladić entered the town of Srebrenica, a United Nations-designated safe area in Bosnia. Over the following days they killed thousands of Bosniak men and boys.
events.significance: It was the worst mass killing in Europe since World War II and was later ruled a genocide. The massacre prompted reflection on the failures of international peacekeeping and led to war crimes prosecutions.
